subject: Pilot engine narrowlist — eval pack, cost/latency/quality notes
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Jenkins <cjenkins@clovertech.com>, Samir Rao <samir@orcahealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-19T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up: Pilot engine narrowlist & next steps

Thanks again for a great demo this morning — appreciate you walking through the integration surface and the throughput requirements. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side: 

- Narrowlist: based on the profiling data you shared and the latency targets (p95 < 180ms for 1k tokens), we recommend shortlisting three engine configurations: Optimized-quant-3 (best cost), FP16-latency-1 (best latency), and Balanced-2 (best overall quality/cost). See attached pilot-eval-pack.xlsx for details.

- Evidence pack: latency-cost-summary.pdf contains baseline runs (1k/2k tokens), batch/seq distributions, and expected per-token unit economics at projected QPS. Prompt-set-v1.jsonl is a first-pass prompt inventory we used for regression checks.

- Key asks from CloverTech: confirm target SLA for the pilot (latency p95 and availability), and share the internal procurement contact so we can start the SOW/PO path.

Next steps: I can consolidate a mutual action plan and a 4-week pilot SOW if you confirm procurement contact and the SLA target. Proposed kickoff: week of 6/28.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.ai

Attachments: pilot-eval-pack.xlsx (spreadsheet, 6 sheets), latency-cost-summary.pdf (7 pages), prompt-set-v1.jsonl (72 prompts)

From: Claire Jenkins <cjenkins@clovertech.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samir Rao <samir@orcahealth.com>, procurement@clovertech.com
Date: 2027-06-19T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Pilot engine narrowlist & next steps

Thanks, Kimberly — helpful recap. A couple quick items from our side: 

- Target SLA for pilot: p95 < 200ms for 1k tokens (we can be flexible if you think 180ms is achievable but would prefer conservative estimates). Availability target: 99.5% for pilot window.
- Procurement: procurement@clovertech.com is our central procurement mailbox (cc'd). They will need an estimate for monthly committed spend and an approximate SOW to start internal approvals.

Could you also call out which of the three candidates has the lowest risk for quality regression given our domain (medical triage prompts)? We can't tolerate drift on safety-sensitive paths.

Claire
Director of Product | CloverTech
cjenkins@clovertech.com

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-19T11:20:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Pilot engine narrowlist — internal eval notes

Attaching the evaluation notes I ran overnight (included in pilot-eval-pack.xlsx) and a short callout on tradeoffs. TL;DR:

- FP16-latency-1: lowest p95 latency in our infra (avg p95 140–160ms at 50 qps for 1k tokens), highest cost (~1.6x Balanced-2). Best if Clover prioritizes latency over unit economics. Lower risk of quality regression vs quant-3 because it's FP16, not aggressively quantized.

- Optimized-quant-3: ~45–55% cost reduction vs FP16-latency-1 at comparable throughput due to 4-bit quant kernels. Latency p95 around 175–210ms depending on hot cache; higher variance for long-tail sequences. Quality: small degradation on rare medical entity completions; needs prompt-level guardrails and regression tests (see prompt-set-v1.jsonl).

- Balanced-2: middle ground. Good quality for triage prompts (meets our accuracy proxies), cost ~1.1x of quant-3, p95 ~160–180ms. Supports our suggested canary gating and automatic fallback to FP16 model variant for safety-critical requests.

Benchmarks & links included in the sheet:
- Benchmark run ids: run_20270618_fp16_50qps, run_20270618_quant3_50qps 
- Perf traces (Drive): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c
- Regression test results (sample): https://docs.google.com/document/d/abc123

Action items for Kimberly: produce a short client-facing one-pager with recommendation and pilot SOW outline. For procurement: ballpark monthly committed spend for pilot = $12k–$18k depending on chosen engine (we should give a tight range for SOW).

Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai

Attachments: pilot-eval-pack.xlsx (see sheet 'benchmarks' and 'regressions')

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-19T14:32:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Pilot engine narrowlist — ops risk & gating notes

Adding an ops perspective — short list of operational risk mitigations I'd want in the SOW and pilot plan: 

1) Canary gating: route 5–10% of traffic to the new engine and measure deltas on latency/error/QA checks before full roll. Automated rollback if quality delta > 3% on our eval set.
2) KV cache priming: add prefix caching for common triage prompts (saves ~35% tokens on warm starts). We'll need access to a 7-day prompt sample to configure correctly.
3) Fallback policy: on repro cases (hit on safety keyword list) or p95 > 220ms, fallback to FP16-latency-1 to preserve availability.
4) Logging & audit: retention 180 days for request/response metadata, masked PHI fields per SOW.

Quantization note: if we pilot Optimized-quant-3, include a supervised regression monitoring plan tied to prompt-set-v1.jsonl and a weekly quality snapshot. That will catch entity-level drop-offs early.

I'll draft the ops section of the SOW and share by EOD tomorrow. Also, we should propose success criteria: p95 < 200ms and mean accuracy proxy (triage label match) >= 94% across the eval set.

Monica Patel
Principal Reliability Engineer | Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.ai

Attachments referenced: latency-cost-summary.pdf (ops appendix), prompt-set-v1.jsonl (for regression checks)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Jenkins <cjenkins@clovertech.com>, procurement@clovertech.com
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Samir Rao <samir@orcahealth.com>
Date: 2027-06-19T17:43:00-07:00
Subject: Next: SOW + pilot kickoff planning (DEAL-3491-CLOVER)

Thanks for the quick responses, Claire. Per Ben & Monica's notes above, here's a proposed concrete path to pilot kickoff: 

1) Recommendation: start pilot on Balanced-2 with automatic fallback to FP16-latency-1 for safety-critical flows. Balanced-2 minimizes initial regression risk while keeping cost near-competitive. If Clover confirms strict latency targets and is willing to accept higher cost, we can switch to FP16-latency-1 in a later sprint.
2) Proposed SOW summary (high level to share with procurement): 
   - Pilot term: 4 weeks (staging + 3-week data & load window).
   - Committed capacity: 50 qps baseline, burst to 100 qps.
   - Expected monthly spend estimate (pilot window): $14k (range $12k–$18k depending on engine selection).
   - Deliverables: pilot-eval-pack.xlsx, weekly quality snapshots, rollback & fallback config, ops runbook.
3) Ops gates: as Monica noted — canary at 5–10%, weekly regression checks against prompt-set-v1.jsonl, automatic fallback triggers.
4) Procurement ask: procurement@clovertech.com — if you can confirm PO routing and any contract templates (NDA already done), we'll prepare a succinct SOW and estimate for signature. We can also provide a DocuSign stub once SOW is OK.

I'll prepare the one-pager recommendation and SOW draft tomorrow and share the HubSpot deal update: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/3491

Proposed dates: Pilot kickoff week of 6/28; first quality snapshot 7/5.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.ai

Attachments: pilot-eval-pack.xlsx, latency-cost-summary.pdf, prompt-set-v1.jsonl
